amenitiesDescription: Casa Cipriani brings its private club model to Miami Beach with an amenity depth unmatched on Collins Avenue. The building houses an indoor-outdoor Cipriani restaurant, a garden bar, a jazz club, and a members-only club lounge available to all 23 owners. A resort pool with full poolside food and beverage by Cipriani connects directly to Mid-Beach's Atlantic shoreline. A full-service spa with sauna and treatment rooms, a fitness center, a screening room, and a library round out the program. Services run at hotel standard around the clock: dedicated concierge, in-home Cipriani dining and catering, 24-hour valet, and continuous security.
architectQuote: Casa Cipriani was designed as a seamless interplay of classic proportions and modern sophistication, echoing the elegance of the grand 1930s-era hotels that line Collins Avenue.

description: The third Casa Cipriani worldwide — and the brand's first ground-up residential project in Florida — arrives on Collins Avenue with just 23 oceanfront residences, 36 hotel keys, and a private members' club for all owners. Brandon Haw Architecture's 19-story tower occupies one of the last remaining oceanfront sites on Billionaires Beach, its form channeling the proportions of Miami's grand 1930s hotels while delivering unobstructed Atlantic views from every residence.

investmentIntelligence.thesis: Casa Cipriani represents the convergence of three rare attributes in Miami Beach real estate: an iconic hospitality brand operating under the private club model, an ultra-limited 23-unit residential count, and one of the last remaining oceanfront development sites on Collins Avenue. The project sits at the northern anchor of Billionaires Beach, three blocks from the Faena District, in a corridor that includes Aman, Rosewood, and The Perigon. At an anticipated entry point of $25 million, pricing reflects the extreme scarcity and the value of built-in Cipriani club membership. BH3 Management's April 2026 refinance signals continued lender confidence in the project, but the underlying thesis is the club model: Cipriani residences trade on access to a specific service operation, not square footage.

investmentThesis:
Casa Cipriani occupies one of the last significant oceanfront development sites on Collins Avenue, at the northern edge of the Faena District on the stretch known as Billionaires Beach. The 19-story tower echoes the proportions and elegance of Miami Beach's Art Deco hotels while delivering a fully modern living experience: soft, curving facade lines and layered terraces that extend the movement of the ocean into the architecture itself. With just 23 residences, density rivals Aman Miami Beach as the most exclusive branded offering on this corridor.

In April 2026, BH3 Management closed a $105 million refinance on the development site, expanding a prior Bank OZK loan: a capital markets signal on the collateral. As of August 2026 the site is fully cleared — the Coral Reef and Patrician hotels were demolished under Florida's Resiliency and Safe Structures Act, the 2024 law that preempts local historic protection for structures deemed non-compliant with current flood codes — with debris load-out finishing and heavy equipment on site ahead of excavation.
name: Casa Cipriani Miami Beach
residenceContent: Each of the 23 residences averages approximately 3,900 square feet and ranges from one to four bedrooms, with direct oceanfront orientation throughout. Ceiling heights reach 10 feet, and floor-to-ceiling sliding glass doors open onto generous private terraces with panoramic Atlantic views. Open kitchens are anchored by custom Italian cabinetry and outfitted with Wolf and Sub-Zero appliances; imported stone runs through counters and finishes. Primary bathrooms feature sculptural standalone bathtubs, glass-enclosed showers, and backlit stone vanities. A unified smart-home system manages climate, lighting, and building security. Select residences offer direct private elevator access.
